set.body: Turn the existing NeuroArchive, NIfTI, BIDS, and standalone seams into the final extraction proof for Z8 without importing domain concepts into the generic kernel. Move the Future-based profile opener into archive-zarr shared code as AsyncNeuroArchiveZarr over AsyncZarr, retaining BrowserNeuroArchiveZarr source compatibility and browser-gzip defaults. Add the explicit JVM blocking-codec bridge needed to exercise portable async opening with JvmGzip, and prove complete profile opening plus cached partial canonical reads over ordinary HTTP on JVM and Scala.js with equivalent metadata, length, shard-index, and demanded-data traces. Extend the pinned Python/nibabel oracle matrix to open each published canonical Zarr array, verify raw stored values and t-z-y-x ordering for uint8/int16/int32/float32/float64, then verify exported NIfTI dtype, raw/calibrated values, affine, shape, timing, BIDS joins, and run the official BIDS validator over each export when available as a required gate rather than claiming compliance from the internal loader alone. Keep the generic standalone consumer dependent only on scalafim-zarr and compile its portable AsyncZarr/cache/writer API on JVM and Scala.js. Record an honest compatibility receipt distinguishing BIDS-compatible export from NeuroArchive Zarr itself being BIDS-compliant. Gates: archive-zarr JVM/JS, dataset-zarr JVM/JS, generic zarr JVM/JS, Python Zarr+nibabel matrix, official validator, standalone published-artifact compile, compileAll/testAll, and requirement-by-requirement Z8 audit. Explicitly defer full qform/qfac/intent/header provenance expansion, S3, catalogs, Parquet, mutable Zarr, and NeuroArchive retention policy to separate work; do not overclaim those as 0.1 behavior.
set.title: Zarr Z8.6: NeuroArchive remote profile and BIDS/NIfTI extraction proof
